home.description: I'm a Staff Astronomer at the The Center for Astrochemical Studies of the Max Planck Institute for Extraterrestrial Physics. I am interested in the star formation process, starting from large scales (molecular clouds) down to the protoplanetary disks. In particular, I focus on using the gas kinematics to understand the physical processes behind star formation. For this I also use astrochemistry as a tool to guide the planification and analysis of observations. Previously I was at the UK ALMA Regional Center in Manchester (UK), with an ESO ALMA COFUND fellowship and later at Institute for Astronomy of the ETH Zürich. Before moving to the UK I obtained a PhD in Astronomy from Harvard University, and before that my BSc and MSc in Astronomy from Universidad de Chile. As a PhD student, I worked as part of the COMPLETE survey with my advisor Prof. Alyssa Goodman.
home.highlight: Interests: Star formation; gas kinematics; interferometry and image analysis; astrostatistics; astrochemistry.

research.title: Dense Cores
research.sub_title: Structure, coherence, and fragmentation in star-forming cores

papers.abstract: A major part of my work focuses on dense core structure and kinematics, including the transition to coherence and how turbulence regulates core fragmentation. These studies connect core physics to the earliest phases of star and multiple-system formation.
